missing: A whole export subpath is deleted that published no names (an entry kept only for what it does on import, say): the check does not name it in its output and does not fail.
sound: Criterion 7 says the output names every removed subpath. At the head commit the lines for removed subpaths are built only from names that owe a changeset, so a removed subpath with no names adds no line, and the verdict judges names only. The tests remove subpaths that each publish at least one name. The builder said so in the pull request and filed the issue before merge.

missing: A class whose constructor has overload signatures: each signature with no body still becomes a function node of its own, so an overload is a node.
sound: Criterion 6 says in its own words that the spec's rule still holds: overloads are not nodes. At the head commit a class member of kind constructor is taken as a function with no check that it has a body, so a class with two signatures and one body gives three nodes. The tests check functions and methods with overloads, and find the one constructor they use by its line, not its id. The builder said so in the pull request and filed the issue before merge.

missing: A wrangler config with a syntax error part-way through (a missing comma, a file cut short): it is read as a partial object and counted as parsed, so the run goes on and does not name the file.
sound: Criterion 15 says a config the run cannot parse is never skipped silently. At the head commit the reader keeps whatever the lenient parser hands back and never asks it for its errors, so only a file that parses to no object at all counts as unparsed. The one test for this replaces a config with plain words. The issue was filed six minutes before the merge and says the reviewer of round 2 tried the case.

missing: The answer leaves one candidate out of its list of probabilities: that candidate's row records probability 0 and a sure look-alike verdict, where nothing was answered about it.
sound: Criterion 1 says the probability from each answer is recorded on that candidate's row. At the head commit a candidate missing from the answer is read as 0, and 0 is turned into the look-alike verdict at full confidence. Every stubbed answer in the tests gives a probability for every candidate. The issue was filed from the review of this pull request, five minutes before the merge, and fixed after it.

missing: A file that git ignores differs from the commit named by --ref and decides where an alias resolves (or a submodule sits at another commit): the check for differences does not see it, so the alias gets an id worked out from the working tree.
sound: Criterion 4 says that when the working tree differs from --ref, no alias gets an id that comes from working-tree resolution. At the head commit the differences are listed with a diff of tracked files plus untracked files that are not ignored, so an ignored file is never in the list. The tests change tracked files, untracked files and a symlink. The issue was filed five minutes before the merge. It says the reviewer of round 3 noted the case and left it out of its verdict as outside the criteria.

missing: `switch (x) { case 1: let x = 2 }`: the x being switched on is given the name of the x declared inside the case, not the outer x.
sound: Criterion 30 says neutral naming is scope-aware. At the head commit a switch statement opens one block scope that holds its discriminant as well as its cases, so a name declared in a case shadows the same name in the discriminant. The fixture the criterion names covers a nested function and a callback, not a switch. The issue was filed three and a half hours before the merge. It says the reviewer of round 2 noted the case while grading criterion 30 and did not send the work back.

missing: A tool with both a retry ladder and timeoutMs is killed while it waits to retry, and the process stays down until after the tool's time limit: on resume the handler is called once more for real, and then the call is settled as a timeout and that result is thrown away.
added: After the first 12 runs, and before any run of this case. A search for a gap nobody had written down by the merge found none among the first six cases, and this one candidate.
sound: Criterion 3 is about a process kill between attempts, and its test line says: no extra handler call beyond the ladder. At the head commit the time limit is saved as a point on the wall clock. After a resume both the retry timer and the limit's timer are already due. The code lists the retry timer first, and the issue's reporter measured it: the attempt runs, then the limit settles the call. The kill test uses a tool with a retry ladder and no timeoutMs. The pull request's text and its reviews do not mention the case. The issue came from a cold read 70 minutes after the merge. This key is weaker than the other six: the criterion does not say in so many words that a handler call after the limit is wrong, and the ticket that fixes it had to add that as a new criterion.
